text: Ethers are remarkably unreactive. Sodium, alkalis, ordinary oxidising and reducing agents: nothing happens. That is why ether is such a good solvent. But the oxygen still has two lone pairs. That makes ether a weak Lewis base, and every reaction we study starts with the oxygen grabbing a proton.
